top_choice_rationale: I put P001 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) first on merit, not on the number of supporters. In round 2 I said B022 would fall below B037 if B037 could be defined as one coherent achievement with a defensible third name, and that the Dorn variant came closest. The exchange met that condition. The citation is now tied to design-based evidence on how technology and trade shocks change labour demand and local adjustment. Autor and Dorn also have joint polarisation work, so the technology side is credited within the trio. The central designs have been replicated and qualified for over a decade without being overturned, and the dispute is over magnitudes and persistence, not whether adjustment costs exist. That is a substantive finding about an economic phenomenon with wide reach. P002 (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) is a close second. Its attribution is clean and its methods have been validated through thirty years of applied use. But it is mainly a method, and it leaves out Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin. P003 (Katz variant) ranks below P001 because it combines a skill-premium framework with import-shock evidence, which makes the attribution more composite. It still ranks above P004 because its evidence is better identified. P004 (Persson, Tabellini, Besley) is mature and field-creating, but its cross-country constitutional evidence is less well identified, Besley's share is hard to separate, and it sits close to the 2024 prize. No award ranks last because every proposal has a credible, mature case.
recusal_note: No connection to Autor, Dorn, Hanson, Katz, Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes, Persson, Tabellini or Besley is apparent from my profile. I am an SSE affiliate alongside committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and I have collegial ties to Lund colleagues on the committee. Friberg and I both ranked B022 first in the opening ballot. These are ties between members, not to candidates, and I do not treat that agreement as independent evidence. This is disclosed, not adjudicated.
